lecture.titre: Why small exporters are rethinking their supply chains
texte: For years, small and medium-sized exporters treated their supply chains as an afterthought. Goods were sourced wherever they were cheapest, and few companies had a plan B when a shipment got stuck at a port.

That mindset is shifting. Rising tariffs, longer delivery times and a string of disruptions have pushed many firms to diversify their suppliers. Some are bringing production closer to home, a trend often called nearshoring, while others are simply keeping larger stocks on hand.

The trade-off is clear: resilience comes at a cost. Holding more inventory ties up cash, and local suppliers rarely match Asian prices. Yet several business owners say the peace of mind is worth it. As one put it, being able to deliver on time has become a selling point in its own right.

vocab.mot: a selling point in its own right

lecture.titre: El fútbol español busca nuevos mercados en Asia
texte: Los clubes españoles llevan años intentando hacerse un hueco en el mercado asiático. Las giras de pretemporada, las academias y los acuerdos de patrocinio se han convertido en herramientas clave para ganar aficionados al otro lado del mundo.
Sin embargo, la competencia es feroz. La Premier League sigue llevando la delantera en audiencias y en derechos televisivos, y los clubes ingleses disponen de presupuestos mucho más holgados.

Aun así, varios directivos se muestran optimistas. Según ellos, la clave está en apostar por el largo plazo: formar entrenadores locales, crear contenidos en el idioma de cada país y no limitarse a vender camisetas.
